section_summary: Pages 167–173 conclude an investigation of a Japanese Navy sponsored mission to Manila in 1944. The report describes the mission’s intelligence aims, its members’ black market and extortion activities, and the investigators’ finding that allegations of killings were unsubstantiated. Pages 174–216 begin a separate survey of Japanese military intelligence in China, covering Army intelligence, special service organizations, and the Kempei Tai.

subfiles.title: Investigation of Hovans's Manila mission, concluding pages
subfiles.about: Investigates the purpose, personnel, conduct, and alleged crimes of a Japanese sponsored mission sent from Shanghai to Manila in 1944.
subfiles.summary: Witness statements describe a mission intended to study Filipino attitudes and gather information, including intercepted radio traffic. Members also engaged in black market dealings, swindling, and alleged extortion. The report finds no substantiated evidence that the group tortured or killed Americans or Filipinos, assesses its intelligence results as slight, and says investigators still sought Hovans for questioning.

subfiles.title: Military Intelligence
subfiles.about: Surveys Japanese Army intelligence structures, operations, personnel, special service organizations, and military police in occupied China.
subfiles.summary: A table of contents precedes a survey of intelligence command and collection in North, Central, and South China. The North China chapter includes a dated 1945-12-02 statement on weak agent networks, limited radio interception, training, and the difficulty of tracking Communist and Soviet forces. Later chapters trace the changing names and duties of special service organizations, profile individual Kikans and regional operations, and describe the Kempei Tai's command, training, jurisdiction, agents, and methods. Pages 212–213 contain duplicate versions of the opening Kempei Tai section; the discussion continues through page 216.
